# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-9 (Extended v90)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to 1826. **Current narrative point (Spring Year 3, harbor town of Dunstead)**: Valjean and Cosette established in convent garden; Valjean working as assistant gardener alongside Fauchelevent; Cosette attending as convent scholar. Key dates: 1815 (Bishop's 75th birthday, Valjean's theft and flight; Waterloo/Hougomont June 17-18); 1817 (young Parisians' Saint-Cloud excursion); 1818 spring (Montfermeil, Thénardier family, Fantine's arrival); 1819-1821 (Madeleine's mayoral tenure); **1823 January (Fantine's arrest; Javert's revelation; TRIAL SEQUENCE in Arras; Valjean's self-revelation; acquittal of Champmathieu; RETURN TO M. SUR M. before six a.m.; Fantine's death; Valjean arrested beside death-bed; VALJEAN ESCAPES same evening)**; December 1823 (Montfermeil rescue of Cosette, 1,500-franc payment to Thénardier); **December 26, 1823 (Valjean and Cosette returned to Paris via Barrier Monceaux)**; 1824 spring onward (decrepit building lodging; winter passed; spring advanced); **Summer Year 2**: Achieved sanctuary inside walled garden compound, le Petit-Picpus district. **Winter Year 2**: Mother Crucifixion died at daybreak; funeral procession completed; vault burial succeeded; **Day after funeral**: Valjean and Cosette integrated into convent life. **Spring Year 3**: Now occurring; described as "spring of the third year."

## Primary Locations
M. sur M.; Montfermeil; **English harbor towns**: Dunstead, Yarlby, Kelford, Ravenmere, Staveford, Ostcombe, Gulhaven, and named individuals (Luvie, Wilwick, Gadrek Prydenridge, Isric, Jotho, Tatho Brackick, Harine Lindmere, Pelde Stenson, Pelde Stenworth, Yera Stenworth, Yewyn Haskick, Orrald the Younger, Davus Stenworth, Ismira Stenson, Movie Prydenridge, Ulrald Corrford, Yedan, Elra Corrford, etc.—rural English community with quotidian activities). Arras; Waterloo; Toulon; Paris districts including Mouffetard quarter. **LE PETIT-PICPUS DISTRICT**: Between Faubourg Saint-Antoine and la Râpée; market-gardens, timber-yards, unpaved roads; roads all ruts and puddles after thaw. **Number 62 Rue Petit-Picpus (CONVENT CARRIAGE GATE)**: Ajar gate, courtyard, vine-hung walls, tall trees above wall. **Wall (approximately 18 feet)**: Extends from niche to house 49 Rue Polonceau; shorter fragment along Rue Droit-Mur. **CONVENT COMPLEX - THREE BUILDINGS**: (1) **Great Convent**: Inhabited by Bernardines-Benedictines nuns; gloomy building, heavily shuttered window with sheet zinc. (2) **Boarding-school**: Where scholars lodged. (3) **Little Convent**: Building with garden housing aged nuns of various orders destroyed in Revolution. **INTERIOR GARDEN (Great Convent)**: Vast oblong area; alley of large poplars; forest trees in corners; solitary gnarled tree, fruit-trees, vegetable beds, melon patch with glass frames, old well, stone benches, grass and green mould. **PARLOR (Great Convent)**: Monstrous lattice of iron bars; behind lattice: barrier of black shutters with yellow beams, always closed. **Chapel**: Window visible from garden; nuns perform reparation/prayer there. **BURIAL LOCATIONS**: Vaugirard cemetery—ancient cemetery with special Prefecture Permission for nightfall burials; Mother Crucifixion's body buried in vault beneath grand altar of convent church (concealed, no government suspicion).

## Jean Valjean's Psychological and Spiritual Development
**ESCAPE EXECUTION**: Hid inside coffin before Fauchelevent nailed upper plank. Demonstrated gloomy talent—understood contracting to fit diameter of escape; could economize breath for hours without dying; possessed composure and coolness contagious to others.

**CURRENT STATUS (Spring Year 3)**: Integrated into convent life as assistant gardener; inhabits old garden hut with Fauchelevent. Works in garden every day, made himself very useful; formerly pruner of trees; knows all sorts of agricultural secrets; turned to advantage—budded ungrafted orchard trees and made them produce excellent fruit. Receives daily visits from Cosette (appointed hour); watches her running and playing at recreation hours; distinguishes her laugh from rest.

**PSYCHOLOGICAL AND MORAL EVOLUTION**: **MEDITATION ON CAPTIVITY CONTRASTS**: Meditated on two places of captivity: galleys (youth)—frightful, terrible, appeared iniquity of justice; cloister (present)—chaste flame of all souls on same hearth. Recalled former companions: wretched, rose at dawn, toiled until night, designated only by numbers, converted into ciphers, shorn heads, beneath cudgel and disgrace, drank no wine, ate no meat except fatigue duty. Contrasted: on one hand miasms, moral pest, literally devouring plague-stricken; on other, ineffable perfume, darkness versus shadow filled with gleams of light.

**CRISIS OF PRIDE**: Before convent, compared himself only to Bishop; regarded himself unworthy and remained humble. For some time past comparing himself to men in general, and pride beginning to spring up. **VALJEAN'S REDEMPTION**: During night meditations, rose to listen to grateful song of innocent nuns weighed down with severities; blood ran cold at thought those justly chastised raised voices only in blasphemy while he, wretch, had shaken fist at God. **WALL AS SYMBOL**: Striking realization—scaling that wall, passing barriers, painful ascent made to escape other place of expiation, now served entrance to this one. Was this symbol of his destiny? House was prison likewise yet never conceived idea of anything similar.

**SPIRITUAL TRANSFORMATION**: In these meditations, his pride vanished. Scrutinized own heart in all manner of ways; felt his pettiness; wept many times. All that entered into life last six months led back towards Bishop's holy injunctions—Cosette through love, convent through humility. Sometimes at eventide in twilight, knelt in middle of walk skirting chapel, before window through which gazed on night of arrival, turned towards spot where sister made reparation, prostrated in prayer. Thus prayed as he knelt before sister. **CONVENT AS SANCTUARY**: Everything surrounding him—peaceful garden, fragrant flowers, children uttering joyous cries, grave and simple women, silent cloister—slowly permeated him. Little by little, soul became compounded of silence like cloister, perfume like flowers, simplicity like women, joy like children. Reflected that two houses of God received him at two critical moments: first, when all doors closed and human society rejected him; second, when human society set out in pursuit and galleys yawning. Had it not been for first, relapsed into crime; had it not been for second, into torment.

## Cosette's Integration and Development
**INITIAL STATE**: Knew nothing; could say nothing. Nothing trains children to silence like unhappiness. Had suffered so much, feared everything, even to speak or breathe. Hardly begun to regain confidence since with Jean Valjean.

**CONVENT INTEGRATION**: Speedily became accustomed to convent. Only regretted Catherine but dared not say so. Once said to Jean Valjean: "Father, if I had known, I would have brought her away with me." Thinks herself Jean Valjean's daughter (natural assumption). Became convent scholar; received new garments (pupil garb).

**VALJEAN'S PRESERVATION**: Succeeded in getting nuns restore mourning suit made her put on when left Thénardiers' inn. Valjean locked up these garments plus stockings and shoes with camphor and aromatics in little valise; procured valise, set on chair near bed; always carried key. Cosette asked: "Father, what is there in that box which smells so good?"

**DAILY INTERACTION**: At appointed hour flies to hut filling it with paradise; adored him because sisters melancholy and he kind; makes comparisons.

## Fauchelevent's Role and Current Status
**Identity**: Old crippled gardener admitted approximately two years previously (1821 or earlier) on Valjean's (Mayor Madeleine's) recommendation after cart accident. Limps; takes nearly quarter hour to traverse short distances; complains of aching back as usual.

**EXECUTION OF PLANS**: Used service door placing Cosette in vintage basket on back, left with deaf fruit-seller in Rue Chemin-Vert. Placed Valjean in coffin; transported in hearse to Vaugirard cemetery with Valjean inside.

**CEMETERY COMPLICATIONS RESOLVED**: At cemetery, Father Mestienne (grave-digger) dead; replaced by "little Father Lenoir" (jug red wine). Grave-digger lost card (cemetery entry authorization). Fauchelevent found card, buried corpse, filled grave himself; porter would return card; conscript wouldn't pay fifteen francs.

**CHARACTER**: Grateful, talkative, excitable; calls Valjean "Father Madeleine"; peasant of Picardy. Perceived generous action as dying man perceives glass good wine; old egoist finding sweetness in gratitude. Air of convent destroyed personal selfishness; rendered good action absolutely necessary.

**TRIPLE SUCCESS**: Won triple success—in eyes of Jean Valjean (saved and sheltered); in those of grave-digger Gribier (who said to himself: "He spared me that fine"); with convent (enabled retention of coffin under altar, eluded Cæsar and satisfied God).

**RECOMPENSE**: Made him happy; much less work since shared; very fond of snuff, found presence M. Madeleine advantage—used three times as much, in infinitely more luxurious manner, since M. Madeleine paid.

**CURRENT STATUS**: Lives in garden hut with Valjean; continues gardening work; sole person aware of Valjean and Cosette's full presence; only known ally and protector. Nuns do not suspect him leaves garden regularly; eyes fixed on God do not spy; nuns occupied watching each other, paid no heed.

## Javert's Pursuit and Investigation Status
**REASSIGNMENT AND REACTIVATION**: When Valjean escaped M. sur M. jail (January 1823), Javert attached to Paris police. Newspaper announced Valjean's death (December 1823); Javert remarked "That's a good entry." Police report concerning child abduction in Montfermeil revived memory; suspected Valjean sought daughter.

**SECRET INVESTIGATION**: Without telling anyone, took coach to Montfermeil; followed mysterious lodger to Gorbeau house; hired room, listened at lodger's door; Valjean foiled spy by silence.

**REASONS FOR SECRECY**: (1) Slightest indiscretion might alert Valjean; (2) Recapturing ex-convict reputed dead magnificent success; (3) Javert had taste for unforeseen.

**PURSUIT ESCALATION**: Old woman suspected lodger intending to leave, warned Javert; Javert waited behind trees with two men at night. **ESCAPE FROM MOUFFETARD**: Valjean cut street lantern rope; Javert found disorder, led astray. Followed from tree to tree; did not arrest hastily.

**CURRENT STATUS** (Spring Year 3): Even when saw Valjean escaped, sure convict could not be far off; established sentinels, organized traps and ambuscades. Free press embarrasses police; arbitrary arrests denounced; police agents afraid of mistakes.

## Narrative Themes and Commentary
Author remarks burial of Mother Crucifixion under altar is perfectly venial offence—one of faults resembling duty. Nuns committed it without difficulty, with applause of own consciences. In cloister, "government" only intermeddling with authority, always questionable. Rule takes precedence over code. Notes danger of pride in comparative virtue; convent contributed completing Bishop's work in Valjean. **AUTHOR'S DIGRESSION ON PARISIAN STREET CHILDREN**: Author describes street child (ages 7-13)—joyous despite no food, shirt, shoes, roof. Roams in bands, lodges in open air, wears father's old trousers, old hat, yellow suspender. Runs, lies in wait, rummages, blackens pipes, swears like convict, haunts wine-shop, knows thieves, talks slang, sings obscene songs—yet has no evil in heart because possesses pearl of innocence. So long as man in childhood, God wills he shall be innocent. Child has own games (hatred for bourgeois), occupations (calling hackney-coaches, letting down carriage-steps, "making bridge of arts"), own coinage ("loques"—rags—with invariable currency in this Bohemia of children). Observes own fauna (lady-bird, death's-head plant-louse, daddy-long-legs, "the devil," fabulous "deaf thing" monster). Possesses many sayings (cynical like Talleyrand yet more honest), indescribable joviality. **TRANSFORMATION THROUGH THEATRE**: In evening, enters theatre and becomes transfigured from street Arab to "titi"—same being endowed with wings. Theatre is ship turned upside down with keel in air; titi huddle in keel. Suffices for him to be there with radiance of happiness, power of enthusiasm, hand-clapping resembling clapping of wings, to confer on narrow, dark, fetid, sordid, unhealthy, hideous keel name of Paradise.
